purpose: Define the public SDK trust-tier workflow in developer-facing command terms without creating a daemon registry or certification bypass.

tiers.developer_goal: Build and test a portable WASM-baseline plugin locally.
tiers.signing: not required for local source proof
tiers.admission_expectation: daemon may admit only if local policy explicitly allows unsigned development packages

tiers.developer_goal: Ship a portable WASM-baseline plugin signed by a publisher key certified by AIII.
tiers.signing: the packaged signer requires an AIII-signed publisher certificate matching the publisher private key and emits an exact-release T1 candidate; signing does not assign a tier
tiers.admission_expectation: the daemon classifies the candidate as T1 only after verifying the pinned AIII publisher-certifier chain, package and manifest hashes, publisher signature, WASM baseline, interface registration, capability policy, and receipts

tiers.developer_goal: Add reviewed native or provider variants to a portable WASM baseline.
tiers.signing: T2 requires a daemon-verified T1 proof plus a separate AIII reviewer attestation for the exact release; public Certified Channel submission is not yet live in this SDK staging release
tiers.admission_expectation: daemon admits only after trust-tier classification, platform match, containment/probe availability, per-invocation capability evaluation, and host-authored receipts

tiers.developer_goal: Use first-party platform-owned native/data-plane providers as platform-reserved exact releases; optional WASM variants may be shipped for compatibility or regression proof.
tiers.signing: T3 requires one AIII platform_release signature and no publisher or reviewer proof; first-party platform release tooling is separate from the public publisher signer
tiers.admission_expectation: target daemon admits only after platform release signature verification, platform policy, per-invocation capability evaluation, containment, lifecycle proof, revocation handling, and host-authored receipts
